title: Descending horn filtration for a four-block ordinal collapse
statement:
Use standard simplices, horns and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial subset means a degreewise subset closed under all simplicial operators; union and intersection are taken degreewise. Let $N\geq3$ and $1<i<N$ be integers. Let $c:\Delta^N\to\Delta^3$ be induced by the monotone vertex map
$$c(k)=\begin{cases}0&k<i-1,\\1&k=i-1,\\2&k=i,\\3&k>i.\end{cases}$$
There exist an integer $m\geq1$, simplicial subsets $K_m\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_1\subseteq K_0=\Delta^N$, and nondegenerate faces $\sigma_j=\Delta^{S_j}\subseteq\Delta^N$ for $1\leq j\leq m$, where $S_j\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N\}$, such that the following hold. The faces $\sigma_j$ enumerate exactly once the faces whose vertex sets map surjectively onto $\{0,1,2,3\}$ under $c$, in nonincreasing dimension, with $\sigma_1=\Delta^N$. Put $n_j=|S_j|-1$, and let $p_j$ be the position of $i$ in the increasing ordering of $S_j$, numbered starting at zero. Then $3\leq n_j\leq N$, $1<p_j<n_j$, the vertex immediately preceding $i$ in $S_j$ is $i-1$, and $n_j<N$ for $j>1$. Under the increasing-order identification $\sigma_j\cong\Delta^{n_j}$,
$$K_j\cap\sigma_j=\Lambda_{p_j}^{n_j},\qquad K_{j-1}=K_j\cup\sigma_j\quad(1\leq j\leq m).$$
The endpoints are $K_1=\Lambda_i^N$ and $K_m=\Delta^N\times_{\Delta^3}\Lambda_2^3$, viewed as subsets of $\Delta^N$.

source.place: HA Lemma 2.4.4.6, proof for i>1, printed pp. 308–309: the surjective-simplex family, pairs obtained by omitting i, attaching horns and terminal inverse horn. This serves the combinatorial subargument in Step 5 of the inner-horn comparison in the inherited operadic-extension branch of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint. Read nonincreasing in the inconsistent ordering sentence, as required by sigma_1 = Delta^N. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical/combinatorial assertion.

proof.text: Using the cited description of a simplex as a weakly increasing map, its image is a nonempty vertex set T. It factors uniquely as the surjection onto T followed by the increasing enumeration of T; thus it is a degeneracy of the nondegenerate face on T. Let S be the finite family of vertex sets mapping onto all four blocks under c. Order its members S_1,...,S_m by nonincreasing cardinality, breaking ties arbitrarily. The full set is its unique largest member, so m is positive and S_1={0,...,N}. Every S_k contains i. Put P_k=S_k\{i}; the P_k are distinct, omit i, and are disjoint from the family S. Define K_j degreewise to consist of maps whose image is neither S_k nor P_k for any k<=j; define K_0=Delta^N. This is cumulative deletion of precisely those pairs and their degeneracies. The degreewise subsets decrease with j; their closure under the operators is checked next.

source.place: HA Lemma 2.4.4.6, proof for i>1, p. 308: definition of the surjective-simplex family, ordering, paired faces, and K_j.

proof.text: The deleted vertex sets are upward closed. A proper superset U of S_k is surjective under c and has larger cardinality, hence is S_l with l<k. For U containing P_k, if i belongs to U then U contains S_k; if i does not belong to U, then U=P_l for the surjective set S_l=U union {i}, with l<=k. Thus a surviving image has only surviving nonempty subsets. Precomposition can only shrink the image, proving that K_j is a simplicial subset. The two new deleted sets S_j,P_j survived in K_{j-1}: the S_k and P_k are pairwise distinct. Every facet F=S_j\{v} with v!=i survives in K_j: it contains i, so is not any P_k, and if it is surjective its smaller cardinality places it after j. All subsets of these facets survive by closure. Conversely every proper subset of S_j except P_j lies in such a facet: it omits some v!=i. Therefore the only images in sigma_j absent from K_j are S_j and P_j, exactly the two images excluded by the cited definition of Lambda_{p_j}^{n_j}. This proves the intersection formula. Restoring sigma_j restores exactly the two newly deleted images, so K_{j-1}=K_j union sigma_j.

source.place: HA Lemma 2.4.4.6, proof for i>1, p. 308: coface closure and the horn pushout calculation.

proof.text: Surjectivity of S_j under c forces a vertex in each of the four blocks. Blocks 1 and 2 are the singletons {i-1} and {i}; a vertex in block 0 precedes i-1, and a vertex in block 3 follows i. Hence S_j has at least four vertices, the zero-based position p_j of i satisfies 1<p_j<|S_j|-1=n_j, and the immediately preceding vertex is i-1 because no integer lies between them. Every S_j lies in {0,...,N}, so n_j<=N. The full set is the only subset of size N+1; consequently n_j<N for j>1. The increasing enumeration identifies the vertex i with position p_j, as used in the intersection calculation.

source.place: HA Lemma 2.4.4.6, proof for i>1, p. 308: the inequalities and consecutive distinguished vertices.

proof.text: For j=1, the only deleted images are the full vertex set and that set minus i. A map has any other image exactly when it omits a vertex other than i; by the cited horn definition, K_1=Lambda_i^N. At j=m, an image T is deleted exactly when c(T) contains {0,1,3}: if it also contains 2 it is a surjective S_k, while if it does not contain 2 then i is absent and T=P_k for the surjective set T union {i}. Conversely each S_k and P_k meets blocks 0,1,3. Therefore a surviving simplex is exactly a map whose c-image omits a vertex other than 2. By the horn definition its composite with c belongs to Lambda_2^3. Since the cited pullback is degreewise, this is precisely K_m=Delta^N times_{Delta^3} Lambda_2^3, as a simplicial subset in every degree.
